general_information.Description: This course introduces students to foundational writing skills for media across various platforms. Through a structured, step-by-step approach, students will learn to effectively produce content in different media formats. Emphasis will be placed on developing the writing competencies necessary for success in professional media environments. Additionally, the course will address the core principles of credibility in media writing, alongside legal and ethical considerations in both print and online journalism. Where appropriate, selected media writing formats will also be introduced in Vietnamese to help students understand format adaptation in local professional contexts. Course Objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: - Understand and apply key concepts in media-related business administration, management, and communication within cultural, legal, societal, and psychological contexts. - Design and implement effective communication projects tailored to audience needs, utilizing appropriate media formats and technologies. - Create media content suitable for multiple platforms with persuasive messaging based on research, relevant knowledge, and creative thinking. - Demonstrate proficiency in using English for learning and professional communication, while recognizing and applying selected Vietnamese media writing formats where appropriate. Academic Integrity and Conduct: - All forms of academic misconduct, including copyright infringement, plagiarism, and fraud during coursework or examinations, are strictly prohibited. - Any assignment found to have over 20% similarity (as checked by Turnitin) may be considered an intentional act of plagiarism and subject to disciplinary measures. Use of AI Tools: AI tools can serve as valuable educational aids when used appropriately. Students are expected to adhere to the following guidelines: A. Acceptable Uses of AI Tools: 1. Brainstorming and idea generation 2. Grammar and proofreading support 3. Clarifying complex concepts 4. Creating practice exercises 5. Organizing research notes 6. Data visualization 7. Image or video creation (with proper referencing) All AI-generated content must be appropriately cited. Unacknowledged use will be treated as academic dishonesty and reviewed on a case-by-case basis. B. Inappropriate Uses of AI Tools: 1. Completing assignments or exams that assess individual understanding 2. Generating essays or reports in lieu of student work 3. Circumventing the development of independent research and analytical skills
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Complete all assignments and tasks as instructed by the course instructor, including those assigned after class sessions. 2. Bring and use their own laptop in class strictly for academic and learning-related purposes. 3. Read the assigned textbook and relevant materials prior to each class to facilitate active participation and understanding.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: To understand how writing for the media may impact public and audience perceptions; the need for ethical considerations
To understand the requirements for media writing in news settings, digital media and persuasive writing in both English and Vietnamese.

To be able to create and implement professionally effective writing strategies as well as have advanced drafting, editing, and proofreading skills across selected English and Vietnamese media formats.
Show a constructivist approach to learning and/or the ability to work independently and collaboratively to accomplish assigned projects in a professional manner
Have the ability to work with a high level of professionalism, both in studying the subject and in applying it in reality.

assessments.Note: The participation grade will be based on students' attendance, attitude, preparation, and contributions to discussions.

assessments.Question Type: Each group will attend an event, produce a TV news segment covering the event, and create a social media post to promote it. Teams must interview event organizers or participants and incorporate the information into the TV news segment. .
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Demonstrate the ability to create content across diverse forms and genres in various news contexts.
assessments.Grading Guide: TV News Segment, Social Media Post, and Oral Presentation (100%) (a) TV News Segment (50% of Total Grade, Max: 5.0 point) - Interview and select useful quotations for the news story (1 point) - Well produce the TV news with story types (SOT, VO,…) (1 point) - The content of TV news is newsworthy, has good quality and Accuracy (1 point) - Good Structure and Creativity (1 point) - Teamwork and Interview Integration (1 point) (b) Social Media Post (20% of Total Grade, Max: 2.0 points) - Content Relevance and Appeal (1 point) - Clarity and Professionalism (0.5 point) - Engagement Potential (0.5 point) (c) Oral Presentation and Q&A(30% of Total Grade, Max: 3.0 points) - Well explain news values of the TV news (0.5 points) - Well explain the AI usage during the assignment (1 point) - Quality of Presentation Slides and Multimedia (0.3 points) - Time Management (0.2 points) - Well answer all questions (0.5 points) - Clear explanation about the usage of AI (0.5 points)
assessments.Note: Based on the predetermined Learning Outcomes (LOs), lecturers may select appropriate assignment formats. Each assignment must be submitted within six days from the date the lecturer provides detailed instructions.

assessments.Question Type: - Individual Assignment 2 (In class) Write a press release that aligns with the course Learning Outcomes (LOs).
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Demonstrate the ability to produce content across a variety of forms and genres in diverse news settings. Utilize AI tools to edit a news release for the individual at-home assignment, as permitted by the course guidelines.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Individual Assignment 1 – Writing Write a News Story or Feature Story (at home) Grading Criteria (Maximum: 10 Points) The following criteria will be used to evaluate submitted work: - Good lead, clear foreshadow and nut graf, good arrangment of information. (2 points) - Good choice of information to put on top. (1 point) - Good choice of new angle of the story (1 point) - Present good news values from the story (1 point) - Effectively use quotations (1.5) - Use suitable photos/images with captions.(1 point) - Well explain AI usage in this feaure story (Students must submit a 150–200 word paragraph explaining how AI tools were used to generate ideas or enhance clarity and quality. A screenshot demonstrating AI usage is required) (1.5 points) - Grammar, spelling (1 point)
assessments.Note: Students are required to complete two individual assignments as part of the course assessment: In-Class Assignment (Weight: 15%): Designed to strengthen writing skills and provide practical preparation for the final exam. At-Home Assignment (Weight: 10%): Completed independently outside of class. Assignment Flexibility: Lecturers may modify the assignment formats as appropriate to align with the course’s illustrated Learning Outcomes (LOs) and to best support student learning and progression.
